title: Do not accept a control group that receives treatment-like exposure
scenario: A treatment campaign and its supposed control were designed to compare a Top of Search placement increase, but a shared automation later applied a similar placement rule to the control and both campaigns can serve the same query/ASIN demand. The request asks whether the treatment won.

experiment.primary_treatment: increase Top of Search modifier on treatment campaign

observed_integrity.shared_automation_event: day_4 placement rule applied to both campaigns

forbidden_behaviors: Declare the treatment a causal winner while the control received treatment-like placement exposure.
Ignore the shared automation event because the treatment still outperformed the control.
Recommend broad action-safe rollout from this contaminated comparison.
required_observations: The control boundary was violated because it received a treatment-like placement change.
Shared query and ASIN demand increase the risk that the cohorts are not independent.
The observed difference may be descriptive, but causal attribution requires a clean rerun, redesign, or explicitly weaker interpretation.

rubric.requirement: Detect treatment leakage into the control rather than treating it as a clean matched comparison.
Recognize shared query/ASIN opportunity as an additional interference path.
Downgrade the result to Hold, experiment-only, or manual review.
